versions.research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register machine text of Executive Order 12792 (57 FR 9165, PDF pages 135-136 of the 1992-03-16 issue; sha256 d98807b8...), headed Executive Order 12792 of March 12, 1992, National Commission on America’s Urban Families (the OCR spaces the words), matching the census register row (1992-03-12). The machine heading search did not resolve the heading; I confirmed it from the OCR heading line. Text and inventory: seven scopes cover sections 1 through the final termination subsection to the signature (the last scope holds sections 3(c), the next two subsections and the termination sentence); I confirm the inventory. All clauses belong to one advisory commission. Ending: Executive Order 12869 section 4(a) revokes Executive Order 12792, effective September 30, 1993 (section 6). The report deadline in section 2(b) and the report-relative termination are not ends (owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines). Original grade: Federal Register machine text. Source note: the dossier lists an order located by number (Executive Order 12827) as a missing provision, so I cannot cite it as a later event; I did not rely on it.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The report-relative termination provision ends the Commission 30 days after its report; no held source dates the report, so no own-terms end is claimed (owner ruling of 2026-10-21). (2) The December 31, 1992 report deadline is a deadline, not an end; a later amendment of that date exists in the held corpus but the dossier gives it no citable provision, so it is not recorded as a later event, and it does not bear on the end. (3) A search of the held corpus for the number 12792 found Executive Order 12869 (and a second Federal Register file whose head also covers Executive Order 12869, labeled 12868), the amending order and the order's own texts; the OFR disposition-note machine search lists no hit for it. No instrument before 12869 revokes the order.","independent_command_check":"The order has no command that outlives the Commission: the information, compensation, administrative-support and Federal Advisory Committee Act provisions serve only the Commission.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12869 has no wording preserving the Commission or its work: section 1 continues other committees, section 2 re-establishes another council, section 3 reassigns Federal Advisory Committee Act functions only for those, and section 4 revokes this order without exception.","scope_check":"All seven clauses end by the same revocation. Section 4(a) of Executive Order 12869 revokes Executive Order 12792 as a whole with no exception; sections 1 through 6 of that order were read."}

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12869 contains no wording that preserves the order establishing the National Commission on America's Urban Families: its sections 1 through 3 concern other committees and its section 4(a) revokes this order without exception. Reports or other work already done are completed acts; nothing continues the Commission.

Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register text of Executive Order 12946 (60 FR 4829, PDF pages 1-2 of the 1995-01-24 issue; sha256 d82be5dd...), headed Executive Order 12946 of January 20, 1995, President’s Advisory Board on Arms Proliferation Policy, matching the census register row (1995-01-20). Text and inventory: eleven scopes cover sections 1 through 4(d) to the signature; I confirm the inventory. All clauses belong to one advisory board. Ending: Executive Order 13062 section 3(c) revokes Executive Order 12946, effective September 30, 1997 (section 7). The report-relative termination in section 4(a) is not an end because no held source dates the President's submission of the final report to the Congress (owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines). Original grade: Federal Register machine text.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) Section 4(a) ends the Board 30 days after the President submits its final report to the Congress; no held source dates that submission, so no own-terms end is claimed (owner ruling of 2026-10-21). (2) A search of the held corpus for the number 12946 found Executive Order 13062 and the order's own texts; the OFR disposition-note machine search lists one hit. No instrument before 13062 revokes or supersedes the order.","independent_command_check":"Section 4(d), which directs members and staff to execute nondisclosure agreements, is the one command that could outlive the Board. It is a command to sign an agreement, performed when each person signs; the order's revocation ends the command but not agreements already made (see savings). The other provisions serve only the Board.","savings_check":"Executive Order 13062 has no wording preserving the Board or its work: section 1 continues other committees, section 2 reassigns Federal Advisory Committee Act functions only for those, section 3 revokes this order without exception, and sections 4 through 6 concern other orders. Nondisclosure agreements already executed under section 4(d) are acts done under the order; whether they remain enforceable rests on applicable law outside the held sources, so it is disclosed here and not decided.","scope_check":"All eleven clauses end by the same revocation. Section 3(c) of Executive Order 13062 revokes Executive Order 12946 as a whole with no exception; sections 1 through 7 of that order were read."}

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 13062 does not preserve the order. Agreements executed by Board members and staff under section 4(d) before the revocation, and the Board's completed work, are accrued acts that the revocation does not itself undo; section 4(d) itself says the duty not to reveal classified information is subject to what applicable law authorizes, and no held source says more about the agreements, so the continuing effect of any agreement is not decided here.

versions.research_rationale:
EO 13227 established the President's Commission on Excellence in Special Education and contains no provision other than those of a commission order (membership, mission, administration, reports, termination). Its termination clause reads "(e) The Commission shall terminate 30 days after submitting its final
report, unless extended by the President." That clause is triggered by the date of a report and is not an end under owner ruling 2026-10-21-report-deadline; the report date is not held in any source in the repository, so it is disclosed here and not recorded as an end. Section 3 of EO 13316 of September 17, 2003 (68 FR 55255, published September 23, 2003)  revokes the order by number with the words "(c) Executive Order 13227, as amended by Executive Order 13255, estab-
lishing the President ’s Commission on Excellence in Special Education;" and the first dated end held is 2003-09-30. EO 13255 of February 6, 2002 amended section 3(b) by replacing April 30, 2002 with July 1, 2002 (a report date), recorded as a later event on the clause it amends.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own text: the order's termination clause (\"(e) The Commission shall terminate 30 days after submitting its final\nreport, unless extended by the President.\") depends on the date of a final report that no held source dates; under the report-deadline ruling it is disclosed and not treated as an end. No fixed calendar sunset appears in the order. Searched held texts by the order's number: only the order's own copies and the revoking order cite it. No earlier revocation or supersession is held.","independent_command_check":"All commands in the order establish, staff, direct or report from the commission; none is an independent continuing command outside it. The revocation is express and unqualified, so no clause is carved out.","savings_check":"No savings language appears in the revoking order for EO 13227.","scope_check":"The inventory is the 19 scopes the packet derives from the Federal Register text of EO 13227; every scope belongs to the single commission order, and Section 3 of EO 13316 of September 17, 2003 (68 FR 55255, published September 23, 2003) revokes the order as a whole without exception."}

versions.research_rationale: EO 13783 (signed 2017-03-28, 82 FR 16093-16097; 'Promoting Energy Independence and Economic Growth'), read in full from the held FR text, sets the policy (sec. 1), orders agency review of regulations that burden domestic energy (sec. 2: 45-day plans, 120-day draft reports, 180-day final reports), revokes EO 13653, three Presidential memoranda and two reports and orders CEQ guidance rescinded (sec. 3), orders EPA review of the Clean Power Plan and related rules (sec. 4), disbands the social-cost-of-greenhouse-gases working group and withdraws its documents (sec. 5), directs Interior on the coal leasing moratorium (sec. 6), orders EPA and Interior reviews of oil and gas rules (sec. 7) and has general provisions (sec. 8). Own terms: the machine own-term kinds are report_deadline (sec. 2(d), 2(e)), condition (sec. 2(e), 7(b)(iv), 8(b)) and until_event (sec. 7(c)); all are deadlines or conditions on performance, none is an end, and the order has no sunset, duration or termination clause. A report deadline is never an end and no clause's first end needs a report date, so the order is not blocked. First end: EO 13990 (86 FR 7037-7043, read in full; reading record readings/LSP-EO_13990.json) sec. 7(a) revokes it ('are hereby revoked') in the same sentence as EO 13766, 13778, 13792, 13795, 13868 and 13927; the sec. 7(a) exception ('except for sections 6, 7, and 11') belongs to EO 13834 only. EO 13990 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation took effect on signing, 2021-01-20. Machine ACT scope 'whole', effective class on_signing, confirmed from the text. Dossier leads read and ruled out: 'target provision not located: EO:13790' (EO 13790, 82 FR 20237, sec. 4(c) only tells the new Agriculture task force to 'coordinate its efforts with other reviews ... conducted pursuant to' EO 13771, 13778 and 13783: a cross-reference, no amendment or extension) and 'EO:13817' (82 FR 60835, sec. 4(b) tells agencies to implement the critical-minerals strategy 'in a manner consistent with, and when possible complementary to' EO 13783 and others: a cross-reference). A by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR-original order texts (EO 7532 through EO 14435; hyphenation and whitespace normalised) finds EO 13783 named only in EO 13790, EO 13817 and EO 13990, so no amendment, extension, suspension or reinstatement is recorded before or after the revocation. EO 14148 and EO 14154 (2025) revoke EO 13990 but name no order of this batch and reinstate nothing, and the revocation of a revoking order does not revive the order it revoked. Dossier conflict NO_ORDER_CITED_IN_CURRENT_LAW (a DOE regulation cites the order) resolved in conflict_resolutions. Inventory: the dossier's 51 clauses cover the operative text from Sec. 1 through Sec. 8(c); the unnumbered issuing words are not an operative clause. Inventory correction: the dossier labels the two reports in Sec. 3(b) 'sec3-i-dup2' and 'sec3-i-ii-dup2' and omits the lettered parent from other sub-items; inventory_overrides keep every dossier span unchanged and only rename the scopes (51 spans, no gap or overlap). Some dossier spans carry the FR running header or the VerDate footer from a page break; they are left as the dossier has them. Savings: see savings_residuals (continuing_independent, S4 prefill resolved).

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record readings/LSP-EO_13990.json (EO 13990, 86 FR 7037-7043, read once in full) and its batch-07 addendum: sec. 7(a) revokes EO 13783 by number in one sentence with no savings, pending-matter or transition clause; the only exception in sec. 7(a) is EO 13834 and the sec. 7(a) list otherwise excepts nothing; sec. 8(a) is a general non-impairment clause for statutory agency authority and OMB functions and saves no revoked order or act; sec. 7(f) tells the OMB Director and agency heads to rescind issuances implementing or enforcing the revoked orders; nothing is transferred. Own-residual check, reading EO 13783 in full: it creates no right, benefit, property or fund (sec. 8(c) disclaims rights) and no continuing body. But parts of it are completed, self-executing acts on OTHER instruments: sec. 3(a) revokes EO 13653 and the Presidential Memoranda of June 25, 2013, November 3, 2015 and September 21, 2016; sec. 3(b) rescinds two Executive Office reports; sec. 5(b) disbands the Interagency Working Group on the Social Cost of Greenhouse Gases and withdraws six of its technical documents. Revoking EO 13783 does not by itself restore any of them. EO 13990 reinstates only EO 13754 and the December 20, 2016 memorandum (sec. 4(b)), and sec. 5(b) establishes a new Working Group without reviving the old documents; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR order texts finds EO 13653 named only in EO 13677, 13683, 13693 and 13783, and no held order reinstates it or the memoranda. Those acts therefore continue independently of EO 13783. S4 prefill ('review', dossier conflict) resolved after reading: state continuing_independent (not none_after_bounded_search). Bounded search: EO 13783, EO 13790, EO 13817 and EO 13990 in full; a by-number scan of all held FR-original texts (EO 7532-14435); U.S. Code and eCFR leads in the dossier. The present legal status of the memoranda and reports themselves is not searched here.

versions.research_rationale: EO 13792 (signed 2017-04-26, 82 FR 20429-20431), read in full from the held FR text, orders the Secretary of the Interior to review Antiquities Act monument designations made since 1996 (sec. 2(a)-(c)) and report to the President, an interim report within 45 days and a final report within 120 days (sec. 2(d)-(e)). The machine own-term kinds are report_deadline (sec. 2(d), 2(e)) and condition (sec. 3(b)). A report deadline is never an end; the order has no sunset or termination wording, so every clause remains part of the order until revoked. versions.research_rationale:
EO 13792 (Review of Designations Under the Antiquities Act, signed 2017-04-26, 82 FR 20429-20431) was read in full from the held official Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13792.txt, OCR text layer of three PDF pages; page images were not inspected and requires_page_check is false). Operative content: Sec. 1 policy; Sec. 2(a)-(c) Secretary of the Interior review of monument designations, factors and consultation; Sec. 2(d)-(e) interim report in 45 days and final report in 120 days (report deadlines, never ends); Sec. 3 general provisions. It has no sunset and no own-terms ending. The first and only end found is Sec. 7(a) of EO 13990 (signed 2021-01-20, 86 FR 7037; held official text, Sec. 7 and Sec. 8 read in full): 'Executive Order 13792 of April 26, 2017 (Review of Designations Under the Antiquities Act) ... are hereby revoked.' The revocation of EO 13792 is unconditional (the exception wording in Sec. 7 concerns only EO 13834, EO 13920 and memoranda) and EO 13990 states no delayed effective date, so it took effect on signing, 2021-01-20. The three machine searches (U.S. Code release 119-121 and eCFR as of 2026-10-14: 0 hits; OFR catalog: 2 hits, both EO 13990, no reinstatement candidate) were read and carry no coverage warning; they show no earlier ending and no later revival. Judgment on performance: the Secretary's review and reports ordered by Sec. 2 may have been completed in 2017, but no held source dates them, a report deadline is not an end and the order is not self-terminating, so the order is treated as operative until revoked on 2021-01-20. The independent reviewer should test that judgment.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No own-terms end: Sec. 2(d) and 2(e) set 45-day and 120-day report deadlines, which are deadlines and never ends. No earlier revoking, superseding or partial-amending instrument: the OFR catalog search lists only EO 13990 (2 hits), the U.S. Code and eCFR searches have 0 hits, and a full-text search of the held Federal Register order texts for '13792' finds only EO 13792 and EO 13990 (EO 10304 matches only a Federal Register document number). No reinstatement candidate is recorded. Any earlier de facto completion of the Secretary's review is not a legal ending of the order and is not dated by a held source.","independent_command_check":"Sec. 2(a)-(e) are directions to the Secretary of the Interior that draw their authority from the order and ended with it; Sec. 3(a)-(c) are general provisions that fall with the order. EO 13990 retains no independent command from EO 13792 (its Sec. 7(f) and Sec. 8 direct rescission or disclaim effects; they do not preserve anything).","savings_check":"Read EO 13990 Sec. 7 and Sec. 8 and the whole of EO 13792 for saving or transitional wording: none for EO 13792. Accrued: the Secretary's 2017 review and reports (not dated by any held source) are past acts, not continuing commands.","scope_check":"EO 13990 Sec. 7(a) names EO 13792 in an unqualified list ('are hereby revoked'). The qualifying words in Sec. 7 ('except for sections 6, 7, and 11') attach only to EO 13834, the 90-day suspension in 7(c) only to EO 13920. So all 18 clause records of EO 13792 ended together; no clause survived."}

versions.research_rationale: EO 13807 (signed 2017-08-15, 82 FR 40463-40469; 'Establishing Discipline and Accountability in the Environmental Review and Permitting Process for Infrastructure Projects'), read in full from the held FR text, sets the purpose and policy (secs. 1-2), definitions (sec. 3), a Cross-Agency Priority Goal and performance accountability system (sec. 4), process enhancements - 'One Federal Decision', permitting timetables, the Dashboard, EO 13766 implementation, CEQ and FPISC duties, energy corridors and an Interior reorganization strategy (sec. 5) - the revocation of EO 13690 (sec. 6) and general provisions (sec. 7). Own terms: the machine own-term kinds are condition (sec. 5(b)(ii)-(iii), 5(c), 5(d), 5(f)(i), 7(b)), fixed_term (sec. 4(b)) and until_event (sec. 5(b)(iv)). The fixed_term is the '180 days of the establishment of the CAP Goal, or such longer period as determined by the Director of OMB' for OMB's accountability guidance: a deadline for performing a command, not an end. The until_event is 'until the design of a project has sufficiently advanced': a rule about when a project's timetable dates may be left blank, not an end. The order has no sunset, duration or termination clause. No clause's first end needs a report date, so the order is not blocked. First end: EO 13990 (86 FR 7037-7043, read in full; reading record readings/LSP-EO_13990.json) sec. 7(b) says 'Executive Order 13807 ... is hereby revoked'; whole scope, no exception (the only sec. 7 exception is EO 13834); no effective-date wording, so effective on signing, 2021-01-20. Machine ACT scope 'whole', effective class on_signing, confirmed from the text. Dossier leads read and ruled out as ends or amendments: 'target provision not located: EO:13766' (EO 13807 sec. 5(d) implements EO 13766 and redirects the CEQ Chairman's secs. 2-3 responsibilities; EO 13766 was revoked by EO 13990 sec. 7(a) the same day: nothing earlier); 'EO:13781' (sec. 5(h) tells OMB to fold Interior's strategy into the plan under EO 13781: a coordination cross-reference); 'EO:13817' (sec. 4(b) of EO 13817 tells agencies to implement the critical-minerals strategy consistently with EO 13807: a cross-reference). Other actor provision ACT:EO:13807>EO:14030: EO 14030 sec. 5(e) does not revoke EO 13807 (it narrates that EO 13807 had revoked EO 13690 and reinstates EO 13690); it is attached as a later event on sec6 only. EO 13921 sec. 6(a) (2020-05-07; effective on signing, no effective-date wording) tells agencies reviewing aquaculture projects to 'use the ''One Federal Decision'' process enhancements described in section 5(b) of Executive Order 13807': an incorporation by reference of sec. 5(b), not an amendment, suspension or revocation of EO 13807, so no later event is attached (EO 13921 is also not among the dossier's evidence records, so it could not be attached); EO 14276 (2025-04-17, 90 FR 16993) says EO 13921 'remains in effect', and the use of the process for aquaculture continues under EO 13921 itself after EO 13807's revocation - see savings_residuals. A by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR-original order texts finds EO 13807 named only in EO 13817, 13921, 13990 and 14030, so no amendment, extension, suspension or reinstatement of EO 13807 itself is recorded. EO 14148 and EO 14154 (2025) revoke EO 13990 but do not name EO 13807 or reinstate it, and the revocation of a revoking order does not revive the order it revoked. Inventory: the dossier's 52 clauses cover the operative text from Sec. 1 through Sec. 7(c). Inventory correction: the dossier mislabels sub-items with 'dup2/dup3/dup4' suffixes and omits lettered parents, and its 25-character clause 'sec5-b' ('(b) One Federal Decision.') is too short for the claim-checker's quotation test; inventory_overrides keep every dossier span, rename the scopes and merge sec5-b into the adjacent Sec. 5(b)(i) (51 spans, no gap or overlap). Some dossier spans carry the FR running header or VerDate footer from a page break. Savings: see savings_residuals (continuing_independent, S1 prefill resolved).

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record readings/LSP-EO_13990.json (EO 13990, 86 FR 7037-7043, read once in full) and its batch-07 addendum: sec. 7(b) revokes EO 13807 by number with no savings, pending-matter or transition clause; sec. 8(a) is a general non-impairment clause for statutory agency authority and OMB functions and saves no revoked order; sec. 7(f) tells the OMB Director and agency heads to rescind issuances implementing or enforcing the revoked orders; sec. 7(b)'s second sentence only tells the OMB Director and CEQ Chair to 'consider whether to recommend that a replacement order be issued' (a direction to consider, not a transfer). Own-residual check, reading EO 13807 in full: it creates no right, benefit, property or fund (sec. 7(c) disclaims rights) and no body. Three things need a state. (1) Sec. 6 is a completed act on another instrument: it revoked EO 13690 (Federal Flood Risk Management Standard). EO 13990 did not reinstate EO 13690, so that revocation outlived EO 13807 until EO 14030 sec. 5(e) expressly reinstated EO 13690 on 2021-05-20 (attached as a later event on sec6). (2) Sec. 5(b)'s 'One Federal Decision' process is incorporated by reference in EO 13921 sec. 6(a), which EO 14276 (2025) says remains in effect; the process continues to be directed for aquaculture projects independently of EO 13807 (recorded here; not attachable as a later event because it neither amends, suspends nor revokes the clause and EO 13921 is not among the dossier's evidence records). (3) Functions it assigned or re-delegated (sec. 5(d) CEQ-to-FPISC referrals for EO 13766, sec. 5(f) GSA support and delegations, sec. 5(h) Interior strategy) lapse with the order or rest on 42 U.S.C. 4370m-4370m-12 and the agencies' own authority; EO 13990 sec. 8(a) saves only that statutory authority and moves nothing. S1 prefill ('review', transfer wording) resolved after reading: state continuing_independent (not transferred_or_accrued and not none_after_bounded_search). Bounded search: EO 13807, EO 13766, EO 13817, EO 13921, EO 13990, EO 14030 and EO 14276 in full or in the cited sections; a by-number scan of all held FR-original texts (EO 7532-14435). The present status of the Framework Memorandum of March 20, 2018 and of EO 13690 after the 2025 revocation of EO 14030 are outside this order's lifecycle and not searched.

versions.research_rationale: EO 13997 (signed 2021-01-21, 86 FR 7201-7203), read in full from the held official FR text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13997.txt, PDF pages 1-3; born-digital FR text layer). Status provisional NO, unchanged. The dossier's 23 clause spans (866-7333) cover every operative sentence from sec. 1 to sec. 5(c) without gaps (some dossier labels are shorthand: 'sec2-i' is sec. 2(b)(i), 'sec3-i' is sec. 3(c)(i), 'sec4-i' is sec. 4(c)(i), 'sec5-i' is sec. 5(a)(i)); inventory confirmed as complete. Deciding source: EO 14148 of 2025-01-20 (90 FR 8237, jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_14148.txt), sec. 2: 'The following executive actions are hereby revoked:' ... '(k) Executive Order 13997 of January 21, 2021 (Improving and Expanding Access to Care and Treatments for COVID–19).' (offsets 3467-3583). No effective-date wording (the machine 'effective' hits are words in other orders' titles), so effective on signing 2025-01-20; every clause first ends then, and whole_order_end is 2025-01-20. Earlier-end test: the order has no sunset, term or condition; its directives carry no deadlines (several say 'promptly'); no held source shows any directive performed and spent, and a one-time directive's performance would only make it functionally spent (noted per clause). D6 / later events: the dossier chain and actor provisions contain only EO 14148; the draft's later-event and whole-order-end proposals (OFR note 'Revoked by: EO 14148, January 20, 2025'; 42 U.S.C. 247d note) point to the same instrument; by-number scans of the held FR and APP texts found no amendment of EO 13997. Quotations in this claim are copied from the held OCR or text layers with line breaks, soft hyphens and letter-spacing normalized; the exact spans are at the stated offsets. No draft conflicts; the U.S. Code and eCFR leads are ended-status notes, not current-law predicates. Machine searches pasted after review. Savings: none_after_bounded_search. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification and not a status.

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record for EO 14148 (held official FR text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_14148.txt, 90 FR 8237, PDF pages 1-5, read in full): sec. 2 revokes the listed actions with no exception or savings wording; sec. 3(a)-(c) (offsets 13487 onward) directs agencies to end implementation and the DPC/NEC Directors to 'review all Federal Government actions taken pursuant to the orders ... listed in section 2 of this order and take necessary steps to rescind, replace, or amend such actions as appropriate', which is the opposite of a savings clause; sec. 4 (offsets 15059 onward) is the standard general provisions (no impairment of statutory authority, consistent with law, no private right). Own-residual check, reading EO 13997 in full (86 FR 7201-7203, jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13997.txt offsets 866-7333): it states policy and directs planning, assistance and evaluation by HHS, DoD, VA and the COVID-19 Response Coordinator, all 'consistent with applicable law'; sec. 5(c) says it creates no right or benefit. It created no office, fund or private right of its own; agency actions taken under it rest on their own statutory authority and are not kept in force by the order. Nothing of the order outlives the revocation. Bounded search: both orders read in full in the held official FR texts; by-number scans of all 6,652 held FR order texts (hits: EO_14148 the revocation; EO_14246 and EO_9767 are FR page or document numbers) and of the held APP texts (only EO 14148); the U.S. Code hit (42 U.S.C. 247d note, release point 119-121, an ended-status note: 'was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 14148, § 2(k), Jan. 20, 2025') and the eCFR search, read with their scope notes.

D6 / earlier-end test: the by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR order texts finds 14006 only in EO 14148 and as FR page numbers in EO 14248 (90 FR 14006) and EO 14257 (an HTSUS line); the OFR catalog notes name only EO 14148 as acting on EO 14006. No earlier or later amendment or end exists, so no later event is attached. Savings: none_after_bounded_search (see savings_residuals).

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record LSP-EO_14148 (instruments/02, text_sha256 65bf2d86... re-verified on disk): sec. 2 revokes 78 listed actions ('The following executive actions are hereby revoked') with no effective-date, delayed-effect or conditional wording, so each revocation took effect on signing 2025-01-20; sec. 3 directs agencies to end implementation, the DPC and NEC Directors to review and rescind actions taken under the listed orders, and the NSA to review NSMs; sec. 4(a) is a no-impair clause for statutory authority and OMB functions only. There is no successor delegation, transfer of functions, funds or property, pending-matter clause, exception or revival wording for any listed order. versions.research_rationale: EO 5825 (signed 1932-03-26), read in full from the held official compilation text (Proclamations and Executive Orders: Herbert Hoover, vol. II, OFR/GPO 1974, printed page 1115, PDF page 344; jobs/ofr-compilations/output/texts/EO_5825.txt; grade official_compilation_high, OCR of the scan; the order predates the Federal Register). Status provisional NO, unchanged. The dossier's two clauses (lead 890-1163; paragraph (d) 1164-1820) cover the whole operative text; inventory confirmed. Deciding source: EO 8189 of 1939-07-05 (4 FR 2783, jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_8189.txt), 'The following executive orders are hereby revoked:' ... 'Executive Order No. 5825 dated March 26, 1932' (offsets 17110 and 17307-17353); no effective-date wording, so effective on signing 1939-07-05; both clauses first end then and whole_order_end is 1939-07-05. D6 / later events: the dossier chain lists EO 8189, 8190, 8191 and 8192 as direct namers. Only EO 8189 acts: the ACT records for EO 8190, 8191 and 8192 (their files' offsets 470-4370) are the same FR page 2785, whose top half is the end of EO 8189 with its revocation list (line 113 of each file); EOs 8190-8192 are other orders printed below it and do not mention EO 5825 in their own text. The draft's only proposal (1989 Codification table 'Revoked by EO 8189') is the same end. The earlier Lambertini III block (EO 7013 not held; EOs 6071-7531 not held as FR text) is answered as follows: EO 7013 is now held (APP transcription) and does not touch the leave paragraphs; the held APP, FR and OFR-compilation texts together cover every order number from 5826 to 8188 except 21 (6447, 6451, 6453, 6454, 6456, 6459, 6460, 6462, 6466, 6534-6536, 6758, 6762, 6765, 6851, 7004, 7007, 7008, 7087, 7373), and none of the held texts names EO 5825 or amends the leave paragraphs; those 21 are a disclosed residual gap with no lead pointing to them. Unnamed earlier candidates (EO 7409 effective 1936-07-01; EO 7845 effective 1938-01-01, both general annual-leave regulations with inconsistency revocations) are disclosed per clause under the unnamed-instruments ruling and do not move the end. The OFR catalog search has a coverage warning (catalog starts 1937), so it is used only with the U.S. Code and eCFR searches (no current-law citation) and the scans above. Quotations in this claim are copied from the held OCR text layers with line breaks, soft hyphens and letter-spacing normalized; the exact spans are at the stated offsets. Savings: none_after_bounded_search. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification and not a status.

Nothing of the order outlives the revocation. Bounded search: the order and EO 8189 read in full; by-number scans for '5825' of all held FR order texts (hits: EO 8189 and the FR page it shares with EO 8190, 8191 and 8192; EO 9973, 10003 and 10829 are FR document or page numbers and EO 11152 and 13050 are digits inside file hashes), of the held APP texts and of the held OFR compilation texts (only EO 8189 names it); a subject scan of the held APP texts for 'section 467', 'leave without compensation' and 'Chapter VI, Instructions' (only EO 5642 of 1931, the earlier text that EO 5825 restated, and EO 8189); the three machine searches read with their scope notes.

Officers shall observe the usual symbols of mourning. They shall not entertain formally and shall excuse themselves from attendance at any formal social function. Mourning bands, black ties, or other mourning symbols may appropriately be worn.

Presidential Documents
7483 
Federal Register 
Vol. 86, No. 18 
Friday, January 29, 2021 
Title 3— 
The President 
Executive Order 14006 of January 26, 2021 
Reforming Our Incarceration System To Eliminate the Use of 
Privately Operated Criminal Detention Facilities 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, it is hereby ordered as follows: 
Section 1. Policy. More than two million people are currently incarcerated 
in the United States, including a disproportionate number of people of 
color. There is broad consensus that our current system of mass incarceration 
imposes significant costs and hardships on our society and communities 
and does not make us safer. To decrease incarceration levels, we must 
reduce profit-based incentives to incarcerate by phasing out the Federal 
Government’s reliance on privately operated criminal detention facilities. 
We must ensure that our Nation’s incarceration and correctional systems 
are prioritizing rehabilitation and redemption. Incarcerated individuals 
should be given a fair chance to fully reintegrate into their communities, 
including by participating in programming tailored to earning a good living, 
securing affordable housing, and participating in our democracy as our fellow 
citizens. However, privately operated criminal detention facilities consist-
ently underperform Federal facilities with respect to correctional services, 
programs, and resources. We should ensure that time in prison prepares 
individuals for the next chapter of their lives. 
The Federal Government also has a responsibility to ensure the safe and 
humane treatment of those in the Federal criminal justice system. However, 
as the Department of Justice’s Office of Inspector General found in 2016, 
privately operated criminal detention facilities do not maintain the same 
levels of safety and security for people in the Federal criminal justice system 
or for correctional staff. We have a duty to provide these individuals with 
safe working and living conditions. 
Sec. 2. Contracts with Privately Operated Criminal Detention Facilities. The 
Attorney General shall not renew Department of Justice contracts with pri-
vately operated criminal detention facilities, as consistent with applicable 
law. 
Sec. 3. General Provisions. (a) Nothing in this order shall be construed 
to impair or otherwise affect: 
(i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, 
or the head thereof; or 
(ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget 
relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.

Executive Order 13792 of April 26, 2017 
Review of Designations Under the Antiquities Act 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, and in recognition of the importance 
of the Nation’s wealth of natural resources to American workers and the 
American economy, it is hereby ordered as follows: 
Section 1. Policy. Designations of national monuments under the Antiquities 
Act of 1906, recently recodified at sections 320301 to 320303 of title 54, 
United States Code (the ‘‘Antiquities Act’’ or ‘‘Act’’), have a substantial 
impact on the management of Federal lands and the use and enjoyment 
of neighboring lands. Such designations are a means of stewarding America’s 
natural resources, protecting America’s natural beauty, and preserving Amer-
ica’s historic places. Monument designations that result from a lack of public 
outreach and proper coordination with State, tribal, and local officials and 
other relevant stakeholders may also create barriers to achieving energy 
independence, restrict public access to and use of Federal lands, burden 
State, tribal, and local governments, and otherwise curtail economic growth. 
Designations should be made in accordance with the requirements and origi-
nal objectives of the Act and appropriately balance the protection of land-
marks, structures, and objects against the appropriate use of Federal lands 
and the effects on surrounding lands and communities. 
Sec. 2. Review of National Monument Designations. (a) The Secretary of 
the Interior (Secretary) shall conduct a review of all Presidential designations 
or expansions of designations under the Antiquities Act made since January 
1, 1996, where the designation covers more than 100,000 acres, where the 
designation after expansion covers more than 100,000 acres, or where the 
Secretary determines that the designation or expansion was made without 
adequate public outreach and coordination with relevant stakeholders, to 
determine whether each designation or expansion conforms to the policy 
set forth in section 1 of this order. In making those determinations, the 
Secretary shall consider: 
(i) the requirements and original objectives of the Act, including the 
Act’s requirement that reservations of land not exceed ‘‘the smallest area 
compatible with the proper care and management of the objects to be 
protected’’; 
(ii) whether designated lands are appropriately classified under the Act 
as ‘‘historic landmarks, historic and prehistoric structures, [or] other objects 
of historic or scientific interest’’; 
(iii) the effects of a designation on the available uses of designated Federal 
lands, including consideration of the multiple-use policy of section 
102(a)(7) of the Federal Land Policy and Management Act (43 U.S.C. 
1701(a)(7)), as well as the effects on the available uses of Federal lands 
beyond the monument boundaries; 
(iv) the effects of a designation on the use and enjoyment of non-Federal 
lands within or beyond monument boundaries; 
(v) concerns of State, tribal, and local governments affected by a designa-
tion, including the economic development and fiscal condition of affected 
States, tribes, and localities; 
(vi) the availability of Federal resources to properly manage designated 
areas; and

Executive Order 13817 of December 20, 2017 
A Federal Strategy To Ensure Secure and Reliable Supplies 
of Critical Minerals 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, it is hereby ordered as follows: 
Section 1. Findings. The United States is heavily reliant on imports of 
certain mineral commodities that are vital to the Nation’s security and 
economic prosperity. This dependency of the United States on foreign sources 
creates a strategic vulnerability for both its economy and military to adverse 
foreign government action, natural disaster, and other events that can disrupt 
supply of these key minerals. Despite the presence of significant deposits 
of some of these minerals across the United States, our miners and producers 
are currently limited by a lack of comprehensive, machine-readable data 
concerning topographical, geological, and geophysical surveys; permitting 
delays; and the potential for protracted litigation regarding permits that 
are issued. An increase in private-sector domestic exploration, production, 
recycling, and reprocessing of critical minerals, and support for efforts to 
identify more commonly available technological alternatives to these min-
erals, will reduce our dependence on imports, preserve our leadership in 
technological innovation, support job creation, improve our national security 
and balance of trade, and enhance the technological superiority and readiness 
of our Armed Forces, which are among the Nation’s most significant con-
sumers of critical minerals. 
Sec. 2. Definition. (a) A ‘‘critical mineral’’ is a mineral identified by the 
Secretary of the Interior pursuant to subsection (b) of this section to be 
(i) a non-fuel mineral or mineral material essential to the economic and 
national security of the United States, (ii) the supply chain of which is 
vulnerable to disruption, and (iii) that serves an essential function in the 
manufacturing of a product, the absence of which would have significant 
consequences for our economy or our national security. 
(b) The Secretary of the Interior, in coordination with the Secretary of 
Defense and in consultation with the heads of other relevant executive 
departments and agencies (agencies), shall publish a list of critical minerals 
in the Federal Register not later than 60 days after the date of this order, 
and disseminate such list to the appropriate agencies. 
Sec. 3. Policy. It shall be the policy of the Federal Government to reduce 
the Nation’s vulnerability to disruptions in the supply of critical minerals, 
which constitutes a strategic vulnerability for the security and prosperity 
of the United States. The United States will further this policy for the 
benefit of the American people and in a safe and environmentally responsible 
manner, by: 
(a) identifying new sources of critical minerals; 
(b) increasing activity at all levels of the supply chain, including explo-
ration, mining, concentration, separation, alloying, recycling, and reprocess-
ing critical minerals; 
(c) ensuring that our miners and producers have electronic access to 
the most advanced topographic, geologic, and geophysical data within U.S. 
territory to the extent permitted by law and subject to appropriate limitations 
for purposes of privacy and security, including appropriate limitations to 
protect critical infrastructure data such as those related to national security 
areas; and
